Hello, denizens of /v/guns. @Atko just transferred the subverse to me a few minutes ago, but I've been mulling this post over for a few days now. First, a little about myself: I was born and raised in Kentucky and have been involved with the shooting sports since I was 4 years old. I have an extensive collection of rifles and a somewhat less extensive collection of handguns, and have a CCW for my state. I own and enjoy shooting weapons of all types, from cap-and-ball black powder revolvers through the modern AR platform, and I'll likely be pushing my collection back in time to flintlocks later this year.

I'd like to put forward some new rules and moderation policies for the community to discuss. It's my intention to aggressively limit moderator abuse, so I will be attempting to write the rules in such a way that they can't be bent to justify a moderator's abuse. I would also like to write the rules to keep up quality content and avoid completely worthless shitposts clogging up the subverse. To that end, here is my proposed list of rules.

SUBSCRIBER RULES:

  1. All content MUST be related directly to firearms or the culture surrounding them. For our purposes, a firearm is defined as a device that uses rapidly expanding gases to launch a projectile. Size doesn't matter, so this includes everything from your AR to a naval cannon.

  2. No memes, image macros, or reaction gifs are allowed. [Note: These are still allowed in comments, but if it gets stupid as the sub grows, we might weed them out from there as well.]

  3. Violation of the global user agreement will not be tolerated.

  4. Disagreements will occasionally be heated, and that's fine. Repeated personal attacks upon or harassment of a user across different unrelated threads are not fine. [Note: Try to keep arguments civil, and if you feel it getting uncivil, just walk away for a while until you cool off.]

  5. No spam. If you want to promote your personal site, blog, or company, then make sure you participate EXTENSIVELY in other posts as part of this community. The account of the Tennessee Arms Company on Reddit is a good example of commercial members of the industry participating in a community in a way that betters both the community and the company.

  6. Breaking any of the preceding rules will result in post or comment removal. Repeated violations over a period of time may be met with a total account ban from the community.

Of course, the moderators will be constrained by their own set of rules, which I will post below. Being a moderator in this subreddit will mean being held to a higher standard than normal posters. Repeated, documented violations of the moderator rules will result in their removal, and trust me, I am not shy about removing problematic mods. An interaction with a mod in their official capacity should almost be like an interaction with a robot: Rule gets pasted in a reply, post gets removed, everyone moves on with their life.

MODERATOR RULES:

  1. Moderators will follow all normal rules.

  2. When removing a post or comment, moderators will copy and paste the rule violation that led to the removal in a reply.

  3. Moderators will not take any action whatsoever if a rule from the sidebar is not violated.

  4. Bans must be discussed among moderators. A single moderator cannot ban someone without talking to the other moderators.

  5. Moderators will maintain active accounts. Inactive moderators who haven't posted or spoken with another moderator in 30 days will be removed.

  6. Moderators will not personally attack, harass, or otherwise be complete dicks to members, either during normal conversation or while carrying out their duties.

  7. A pattern of repeated violations of these moderation policies will result in moderator removal at the discretion of the head moderator. All violations should be recorded with a screenshot and sent via PM to the head moderator, @Thjoth.

So, I think that's quite enough out of me for now. Please discuss these rules, I will be actively reading your suggestions and replies until the final version of these go into effect at the end of the week. I'm looking forward to fostering this community along with all of you, and an ironclad set of community and moderation guidelines is essential to keep the quality up and the community healthy.

Well, you and I may agree that karma is worthless, but not everyone does. I think it genuinely affects some people’s sense of self-esteem. Not just karma but any kind of fake internet point: Twitter followers, Facebook friends, Tumblr reblogs, YouTube views, or even levels or money in online games.

Some of these things do have tangible benefits (more Twitter followers means your content reaches more people by default), but then it gets distorted into a measure of power; it feeds their ego.

We don’t have to assume this. You can observe when people go nuts over lost points — so much drama when people get downvoted, or lose followers. And when they gain points their behaviour changes; they are better than others, their opinion is worth more, they deserve to be exempt from rules. Users who say “I have 1 gazillion karma, why am I banned?” instead of “I posted this, which is not forbidden; why am I banned?”.

Somewhat tangential to the topic, but another telling sign that some people value karma: new users on Voat who complain about the CCP threshold for downvoting, or the daily upvote limits. You can remind them that the points don’t matter, but they won’t get it (don’t mean to link to a thread with myself in it, but that’s the first example I could find easily).

Anyway, I don’t think you are missing out on anything. If you do not care for karma then you are a more grounded, real person than many others.
